newTopics.title: Ancient Egypt: Art Made to Last Forever
newTopics.summary: Egyptian artists made objects for the afterlife, so they used strong, simple shapes and lasting materials. Even a small blue hippo could carry big meaning.
keyConcepts: Symbols from nature (the Nile, plants, animals)
Rules that lasted thousands of years
newTopics.tryIt: Design a small animal 'helper' for a journey. Decorate it with symbols of where it lives, the way the hippo's body is covered with river plants.

resources.title: Hippopotamus ("William")
resources.creator: Egypt, Middle Kingdom, ca. 1961–1878 B.C. (faience)
resources.note: Look closely: lotus flowers and river plants are painted on its body — it carries its home with it.

resources.title: How William the Hippo Got His Name
resources.creator: Isabel Stünkel and Kei Yamamoto
resources.note: The story of the museum's favorite hippo and how it got its nickname. Ages 10+.

newTopics.title: The Renaissance: A New Way of Seeing
newTopics.summary: In 15th-century Italy, artists studied people, nature and space more closely than ever. Perspective and soft, believable light made paintings feel like windows.
newTopics.tryIt: Draw a figure in front of a window that shows a landscape. Make the faraway hills smaller and paler than the figure.

resources.title: Madonna and Child
resources.creator: Filippino Lippi, ca. 1483–84
resources.note: Notice the open window and the deep landscape behind the figures — a Renaissance favorite.

resources.title: How one-point linear perspective works
resources.creator: Dr. Beth Harris and Dr. Steven Zucker
resources.note: How Renaissance artists invented a system for painting deep space.

newTopics.title: Impressionism: Painting Light and Moments
newTopics.summary: The Impressionists painted quickly, often outdoors, to catch light as it changed. Loose brushstrokes and bright color showed a moment, not every detail.
newTopics.tryIt: Paint or draw the same object in the morning and in the evening. What happened to the colors?

resources.title: Water Lilies
resources.creator: Claude Monet, 1906
resources.note: No horizon, no sky — just water, reflections and floating flowers.

resources.title: Impressionism: Art and Modernity
resources.creator: Margaret Samu
resources.note: How a group of painters broke the rules in 1874 and changed art. Ages 12+.

newTopics.title: Chinese Landscape Painting: Mountains, Mist and Mind
newTopics.summary: Chinese landscape painters didn't copy one view. They gathered memories of mountains, trees and water into a journey the viewer travels with their eyes.
keyConcepts: Brush and ink as the main tools
Landscape as a mirror of the mind
newTopics.tryIt: Draw a landscape in a long, narrow strip. Put tiny travelers on a path, and leave misty empty spaces between the mountains.

resources.title: Old Trees, Level Distance
resources.creator: Guo Xi, China, Northern Song dynasty, ca. 1080 (handscroll, ink and color on silk)
resources.note: Follow the river from right to left, the way a handscroll is unrolled.

resources.title: Landscape Painting in Chinese Art
resources.creator: Department of Asian Art
resources.note: How landscape became the most important subject in Chinese painting. Ages 12+.
